items.desc: ripe red strawberry with its leafy cap, seen from the side
items.note: Strawberries wear their seeds on the outside, about 200 each

items.desc: classic clear glass incandescent light bulb with a glowing coiled filament and a silver screw base
items.note: Most of the energy in an old bulb came out as heat, not light

items.desc: emperor penguin standing upright, black back, white belly, yellow-orange patch at the neck
items.note: Emperor penguins can dive deeper than 500 metres

items.desc: retro chrome two-slot toaster with two slices of toast popping up
items.note: Sliced bread came after the pop-up toaster, not before

items.desc: garden snail with a brown spiral shell and both eye stalks raised
items.note: A snail can sleep for up to three years in a dry spell

items.desc: desk globe of the Earth on a tilted brass half-ring stand with a wooden base, blue oceans
items.note: The oldest surviving globe, from 1492, has no Americas on it

items.desc: wooden A-frame step ladder, opened, three-quarter view
items.note: Walking under a ladder was unlucky because of the triangle it makes with the wall

items.desc: single tall sunflower head with yellow petals and a dark brown seed centre, short stem
items.note: A sunflower head is hundreds of tiny flowers packed in spirals

items.desc: wooden skateboard with red wheels, tilted three-quarter view showing the deck and trucks
items.note: Skateboards began as surfers' way to surf on dry days

items.desc: small white sailboat with one tall triangular sail and a blue hull
items.note: A sailboat can sail faster than the wind that pushes it

items.desc: tall golden concert harp with its curved neck and many strings
items.note: A concert harp has 47 strings and 7 pedals

items.desc: glass French press coffee maker with a silver plunger and frame, half full of coffee
items.names: french press, cafetiere, coffee press, press pot, plunger
items.note: The plunger's mesh traps the grounds at the bottom

items.desc: narwhal whale with a long straight spiral tusk, grey mottled skin, side view
items.note: The tusk is a tooth, and it can grow 3 metres long

items.desc: carved brown wooden Black Forest cuckoo clock with a little bird at the open door, pine-cone weights hanging on chains
items.note: The pine-cone weights are what keep it running

items.desc: whole red pomegranate next to a cut half showing ruby seeds
items.note: One pomegranate can hold over 600 seeds

items.desc: unicycle with a single wheel, a seat on a straight post and pedals on the wheel hub
items.note: With no gears, one pedal turn is one wheel turn

items.desc: black cast-iron stovetop waffle iron, open, showing the square grid plates
items.note: Waffle irons were once made with family crests on the plates

items.desc: wooden bassoon, long reddish-brown tube with silver keys and a curved metal crook
items.note: Unfolded, a bassoon's tube would be about 2.5 metres long

items.desc: small wooden table loom with warp threads and a half-woven colourful cloth
items.note: The punched cards of the Jacquard loom inspired early computers

items.desc: wooden four-sided spinning top with a Hebrew letter on each face and a short handle
items.note: Each of the four letters tells you what to take or give

items.desc: granite curling stone, grey polished round stone with a red handle on top
items.note: Most curling stones come from one Scottish island, Ailsa Craig

items.desc: red and black snowmobile with front skis and a rear track
items.note: The first snowmobile was built to reach patients in snowy Quebec

items.desc: capybara, a big brown rodent with a blunt square face, sitting
items.note: The world's largest rodent, and a strong swimmer

items.desc: penny-farthing bicycle with a huge front wheel and a tiny rear wheel
items.names: penny-farthing, penny farthing, high wheeler, ordinary
items.note: The big wheel made it faster, since pedals turned the wheel directly

items.desc: ornate brass Russian samovar urn with a tap, side handles and a small teapot on top
items.note: Its central pipe once held burning charcoal to keep the water hot

items.desc: Japanese shamisen, a three-stringed lute with a square drum body and a long thin neck
items.note: It is plucked with a large fan-shaped plectrum called a bachi

items.desc: babirusa wild pig, grey nearly hairless skin, with upper tusks that grow up through the snout and curve back toward the forehead
items.note: Its upper tusks grow up through the top of its snout

items.desc: head of romanesco broccoli with pointed spiralling fractal cones, lime green
items.note: Each cone is made of smaller cones in a spiral pattern

items.desc: surveyor's theodolite, an instrument with a telescope sight on a rotating yellow and black body, standing on a wooden tripod
items.note: It measures angles to map the land, from the pyramids to modern roads
